# HITCON CTF 2026

28 August 2026

Participant qualifier 3 solves NxT, TxN, NxD, DxT

3 writeups

  * Welcome Flag in a markdown comment misc The flag sits in a [//]: # (...) link reference definition, which markdown never renders. Reading the raw description shows it.
  * SPI TPM Free Trial Homemade TPM cipher, HNP lattice attack crypto An aarch64 VM fronts a "TPM firmware" .so that runs natively on x86-64, so the cipher can be studied offline. A 9-bit key-check leak per query becomes a Hidden Number Problem, and the flag blob's own key-check is the 27th leak that makes the lattice solvable.
  * Book of Eclipse One bit flip in IA32_FMASK pwn A kernel ioctl flips one bit of IA32_FMASK. Unmasking DF makes copy_to_user and copy_from_user run backwards, which gives a KASLR leak and a stack return-address overwrite, with extra care because FSRM changes the copy path on the remote.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------

# Kaspersky announces SAS CTF 2026 winners, with Middle East’s PwnSec taking runner-up spot

October 28, 2026

PwnSec from the Middle East secured second place in the attack-defense finals of Kaspersky's Security Analyst Summit (SAS) CTF 2026. The team outperformed competitors from around the world in a 24-hour battle, earning a prize for its impressive performance.

Designed to sharpen cybersecurity skills and strengthen global cybersecurity talent, the SAS CTF 2026 finals, brought together the winners of two competitions – the SAS CTF online qualifiers and Kaspersky{CTF}  –  both completed earlier in the year. Together, the two tournaments drew in more than 2,800 teams and had 14 finalist teams representing Europe, the Middle East, the Asia-Pacific, Latin America and North America.

At this year finals, top cybersecurity talent faced-off in a tense real-time hacking duel, simultaneously defending their own servers while exploiting identical vulnerabilities on rival teams' systems. Scores weren't just about who hacked the most; uptime mattered too, with each team's results multiplied by how well they kept their own services running under pressure. One of the most interesting challenges was a brand-new experiment: an isolated network without AI agents and internet access. Each team had to solve the task using only their own skills and do it manually.

BunkyoWesterns participated for the third time in SAS CTF and this time claimed the top spot and a $10,000 prize. The second place went to Kaspersky{CTF} finalists – PwnSec (the Middle East) with $5,000, and third place was awarded to CUT (Russia) – newcomers from Central University, who took home $3,000.

“SAS CTF 2026 showed us something important: even in an era where AI tools are becoming part of every security researcher's toolkit, there's no substitute for genuine human expertise under pressure. AI can suggest a path forward, but it can't replace the years of hands-on experience and critical thinking our participants demonstrated this year. As AI becomes a bigger part of the cybersecurity landscape, events like SAS CTF remain an important training ground for human talent that will ultimately decide how these tools are used,” comments Leonid Bezvershenko, Senior Security Researcher at Kaspersky GReAT.

The finals were sponsored by Kaspersky Academy and held as part of the 18th annual SAS, taking place October 20-23, 2026, in Bali. The conference gathered over 200 participants from around the globe, with this year's agenda featuring critical vulnerability disclosures and incident investigations into highly complex attacks targeting multiple digital sectors.

To find out more about the SAS 2026, its agenda and speakers, visit https://thesascon.com.

About GReAT

Established in 2008, Global Research & Analysis Team (GReAT) operates at the very heart of Kaspersky, uncovering APTs, cyber-espionage campaigns, major malware, ransomware and underground cyber-criminal trends across the world. Today GReAT consists of 30+ experts working globally – in Europe, Russia, Latin America, Asia and the Middle East. Talented security professionals provide company leadership in anti-malware research and innovation, bringing unrivaled expertise, passion and curiosity to the discovery and analysis of cyberthreats.--------------------------------------------------------------------------------
